title: Crumbs in the Cafeteria
briefing: Someone left a crew terminal logged in by the napkin dispenser. Whoever was last here in a hurry didn't bother locking the session.
prompt: This is a computer terminal -- type a command and press Enter to run it. Try `ls` to list files, `cd foldername` to open a folder, and `cat filename` to read a file. Explore around and see what you can find.
hint: Run `ls -a` -- the `-a` shows hidden files (ones starting with a dot, like `.shift_log`). Then `cat` it.
clue: A shift log left open on the terminal shows the same crew member badged into the Cafeteria twice within one hour -- once more than their schedule allows.

title: Behind the Curtain
briefing: The Admin Office runs a small crew-directory site. It looks harmless, but someone building a website in a hurry sometimes leaves a door unlocked without realizing it.
prompt: Look at this site's address bar. Add `/robots.txt` to the end of the URL and press Enter. This file normally just tells search engines what to skip -- but this one has something extra in it.
hint: Add `/robots.txt` to the end of the URL in your address bar. Scan the lines for anything that isn't a normal 'Disallow' entry.
clue: The hidden staging page still lists the Admin Assistant as the last person to edit the crew directory, timestamped the night of the incident.

title: The Lazy Guard
briefing: The station's security panel was installed years ago. Whoever set it up meant to change the login before going live -- and never got around to it.
prompt: This login panel still has its factory settings -- nobody ever changed them. Try logging in with the most common default username and password combo you can think of.
hint: Username: `admin`. Password: the laziest option -- same word, plus simple initial 3 numbers on the end.
clue: The dumped session log shows the Security Officer disabled the corridor camera outside the Lab twelve minutes before the incident was reported.

title: The Locked Crate
briefing: A supply crate in the bay has a label stamped in a string of letters and numbers -- not encryption, just a way of packing text into a shipping-safe format.
prompt: The crate's label is written in a code called Base64 -- it just hides text, it doesn't encrypt it. Copy the label text and decode it to reveal the real message.
hint: Random letters/numbers ending in `=`? That's Base64. Search 'base64 decode online' and paste it in.
clue: The decoded manifest shows the crate was signed out by the Storage Technician, who had no clearance for lab equipment that day.

title: Whose Birthday Is It?
briefing: The lab's crew-lookup terminal has a photo pinned above it -- two crewmates fist-bumping, names labeled right on the image. The terminal only hands over a sealed personnel file once someone proves they actually know who's in the picture.
prompt: Look at the photo above the terminal. One of the names belongs to a real person you can search for online. Find their birth year, then type just the 4-digit year below.
hint: Sykkuno is a real streamer. Search 'Sykkuno birth year' and type just the 4 digits.
clue: The unlocked record shows the Lab Scientist ran an off-the-books background check on a crewmate the same night, then filed the results under a fake name.

title: Name the Infiltrator
briefing: Every room has given something up. It's time to lay the evidence side by side and decide who's been covering their tracks.
prompt: You've cleared every room! Now go to the Evidence Board, read what each suspect says, and figure out whose story doesn't add up before making your final accusation.
hint: Read what each suspect says on the Evidence Board. One story flat-out couldn't be true given their room -- that's your suspect.
clue: With every room's evidence laid out, the Security Officer is the only suspect whose action has no innocent explanation: disabling the corridor camera outside the Lab minutes before the incident.
